data.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet: An always-on AI agent for your workday
data.description:
Anthropic has launched Claude Duet, an AI agent built to handle busywork for professionals and small business owners. Announced today, Oct. 21, the research preview runs as its own app on iOS, Android and the web, and it is opening first to Claude Pro and Max subscribers in the United States through a waitlist.


Duet is Anthropic’s answer to Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots in a growing race to build personal agents that are always on. Unlike a chatbot that waits for questions, Duet watches a user’s connected apps, sends a short brief each morning and sends a message only when something needs attention.


What can Claude Duet do?

Users can hand Duet tasks ranging from scheduling meetings to building dashboards, drafting financial or sales forecasts, and prototyping web apps. It runs on Claude Opus 5.5, the model Anthropic released in late September.

Duet works on its own cloud computer with a browser, so it keeps going after the user closes the app. It also carries over a user’s memory, skills and connected apps from their Claude account, which keeps setup short.

We’re opening a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent.

It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf. https://t.co/kt8gAbWuX8

— Claude (@claudeai) October 21, 2026

Is Claude Duet safe to use with sensitive information?

Anthropic says Duet asks for approval before big steps such as sending a payment or deleting something. The company also released a new classifier and safety system prompt that check each message. They are designed to block the most sensitive information, such as credit card numbers and government ID numbers. Health and personal financial details pass only when a user specifically tells Duet to send them.

Anthropic says Duet never directly sees passwords or sign-in tokens. The company says internal red teams and an outside firm tested it for security weaknesses, and it is covered by Anthropic’s public bug bounty program.

What are Claude Duet’s limits?

Anthropic calls Duet an early version. The company says it might misread a thread or misjudge what is urgent, and it is not yet as strong at personal errands like booking tickets.

During the preview, Duet draws from the same usage limits as the rest of a subscriber’s Claude plan. Anthropic has not announced separate pricing. Access for Team and Enterprise plans is expected later.

Why is Claude Duet aimed at small business owners?

Duet’s development was led by Karan Ahuja, who ran product management at Meta Superintelligence Labs until July before joining Anthropic in August. He said the team built it for professionals and small business owners juggling a lot at work and at home.

That pitch lands with a lot of people. In communities where so many entrepreneurs wear every hat at once, from the salon owner answering clients between appointments to the side hustler running a brand from a phone, an assistant that sorts priorities and drafts the forecast is a real offer.

How does Claude Duet compare with Meta’s Muse?

Muse has a big head start. Data firm Apptopia estimates Muse had passed 14 million installs as of today. Anthropic announced Duet on the same day Meta reported earnings, and Meta Superintelligence Labs chief Alexandr Wang responded with a meme about how much Duet resembles Muse. Meta also recently paused a Muse sharing feature after researchers found users’ AI chats on the web, a reminder that privacy will shape this race as much as features.

When can you get Claude Duet?

For now, only through the waitlist. Anthropic says it will email users when their access is ready, and Ahuja said the company is letting people in as quickly as possible.

The launch comes as Anthropic approaches an IPO that Business Insider reports could value the company at as much as $2 trillion. The agent is ready to work. The bigger question is how many people are ready to hand it the keys.

data.title: Apple Music changed something after 11 years and fans are furious
data.description:
Apple rarely touches the identity of its biggest apps, which is exactly why this latest move caught so many people off guard. After 11 years with essentially the same look, Apple Music is getting its first real redesign, and the reaction online has been anything but quiet.


The change was quietly spotted buried inside a handful of developer betas, long before any formal announcement, which only added to the sense that something significant was being tested without the usual fanfare.


What Apple Actually Changed

The update starts with the wordmark itself. The tech giant swapped the familiar capitalized Music text for an entirely lowercase version in a much thicker, bolder typeface, giving the logo a wider, heavier feel compared to the slim lettering fans have scrolled past for over a decade. The new look first appeared alongside Apple Music Hall, the company’s new performance venue at London’s Battersea Power Station, before showing up inside developer betas for iOS and macOS.

That alone might have passed as a one-off venue branding choice. Instead, the redesign went further, with Apple testing an entirely new app icon that replaces the signature red background behind the beamed eighth symbol with a stripped-down black-and-white design. A reversed white-on-black version appears automatically in dark mode, and the company has also prepared a tintable clear version that can take on different colors depending on a person’s home screen setup.

Some early testers even noticed the change extending beyond the icon itself, with the red accent color inside the app itself swapped out for a cooler blue tone across menus and buttons, suggesting the redesign runs deeper than a simple logo swap.

Why Fans Are Furious Over the Redesign

Reaction across social media has been loud, and most of it has not been kind. Commenters have called the new icon boring and generic, with some joking that it looks like a design school assignment rather than a finished product from one of the world’s most valuable companies. A handful of people pointed out that the black-and-white treatment does resemble traditional sheet music, offering a rare bit of praise in an otherwise rough reception.

Part of the frustration seems tied to just how recognizable the old red icon had become. Apple Music’s red beamed eighth symbol sat untouched on millions of phones since the service launched, and visual habits like that are notoriously hard to let go of, even when a redesign is objectively cleaner or more modern.

A Pattern of Backlash Whenever Apple Touches an Icon

This is not the first time the company has stirred up this kind of reaction. Apple has a long history of frustrating users whenever it tweaks a familiar icon or interface, only for people to eventually adjust and, in many cases, come to prefer the new look within a year or two. The same pattern played out when the Photos app and Podcasts icons were last overhauled, each time drawing complaints that faded within a few months.

The tech industry is far from alone here either. Instagram faced a similar wave of criticism after changing its own wordmark font recently, and even a rival search giant’s subtle logo tweak a little over a year ago sparked its share of commentary, despite being barely noticeable to casual users. Redesigns at this scale almost always generate noise before they generate acceptance.

What Comes Next for Apple Music

For now, the redesigned wordmark and icon remain confined to developer betas, meaning most listeners have not seen the change firsthand yet. The public website and web player still display the original branding as of this writing.

That is expected to shift soon. The new look is tied to the rollout of iOS and macOS software updates later this month, timed close to the launch of the newest iPhone. Once those updates reach the public, the updated wordmark and icon should appear across the Apple Music app, its website and any related marketing materials, giving millions of listeners their first real look at the full redesign all at once.

Whether the backlash cools down once the design reaches everyone’s home screen, or whether Apple ends up tweaking the icon again before a full launch, remains to be seen. What is clear is that after more than a decade of staying mostly the same, Apple Music’s identity is finally catching up with the rest of Apple’s evolving design language.

data.title: Apple’s iPhone Duo frenzy: Why fans face a 3-month wait
data.description:
Apple fans eager to get their hands on the company’s first foldable phone may need to settle in for a long wait.


The iPhone Duo, which represents the most dramatic redesign of Apple’s flagship device since the original iPhone debuted nearly 20 years ago, opened for pre-orders on Friday, Oct. 16. Within minutes, the device was sold out, and customers who placed orders even half an hour after the launch were told their phones would not arrive until January.


Now the tech giant is addressing the frenzy, and its message for shoppers is to be patient.

A sellout in record time

Anticipation for the iPhone Duo had been building for months, and the pre-order rush confirmed just how eager customers were to try a folding iPhone. At the time of publication, Apple’s website in both the U.S. and the U.K. tells buyers their devices will not be delivered until late January.

There may be a silver lining, however. Apple has a history of offering conservative delivery estimates, which means some customers could receive their phones sooner than expected.

Apple responds to the overwhelming demand

Over the weekend, Apple acknowledged the massive interest in a statement to the Financial Times. The company described pre-order demand as extraordinary and said it is working hard to get the new device to customers as quickly as possible.

Apple also called the iPhone Duo a revolutionary product, signaling how important the foldable model is to its lineup.

Why shoppers should skip the store

Anyone hoping to walk into an Apple Store and leave with an iPhone Duo on launch day may be disappointed. MacRumors reported that retail employees have been instructed to discourage customers from visiting stores to purchase the device when it officially goes on sale Friday, Oct. 23.

According to the outlet, stores will likely have no stock for walk-in shoppers who did not pre-order.

The approach marks a sharp contrast with early iPhone launches, which were famous for long lines that snaked around Apple Stores. Some devoted fans even camped out overnight to secure a new phone. In recent years, Apple has steered customers away from those crowds, encouraging them to pre-order online even if they plan to pick up their device in person.

Why supply is so tight

It remains unclear how many iPhone Duo units Apple produced ahead of the launch or how many it sold during the initial rush.

Even before pre-orders opened, multiple reports had warned that supply could be limited. The phone’s complex folding design is more difficult to manufacture than a traditional smartphone, creating production challenges that may have restricted how many devices were ready in time.

For Apple, the shortage is a mixed blessing. Strong demand suggests the company has a hit on its hands, but long delivery times could test the patience of loyal fans who were ready to upgrade right away.

No wait for the iPhone 18 Pro

The same supply issues have not affected the rest of Apple’s newest lineup. The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which were unveiled alongside the iPhone Duo at Apple’s September launch event, went on sale soon after the announcement.

Both models are still available for immediate purchase, giving shoppers who are not set on a foldable phone an easier path to a new iPhone this fall.

What buyers can expect next

For now, customers who already placed pre-orders will need to keep an eye on their order status for any updates on delivery dates. Those who missed the first wave can still order the device online, though they should be prepared for a wait that could stretch into the new year.

Whether Apple can speed up production before the holidays remains to be seen.

Source: The Independent

data.title: Will the PS6 cost $1,000? Sony weighs a risky price
data.description:
Will the PlayStation 6 launch near $1,000, and what has Sony actually said? The company has not announced the console, its release date or its price. What it has made clear is that rising memory costs are shaping the decision.


What Sony has told investors

At a June 5 investor meeting, Sony said it is not realistic to absorb all component cost increases and that it has already raised some prices outside Japan. It said sales are proceeding as planned and that it does not see a drop in demand. As a principle, it does not intend to sell hardware at significant losses. Sony also said it is monitoring the market and wants customers to understand the value they get for the price.


The word significant leaves room for small losses on each console, but a heavily subsidized launch looks harder to sustain. Sony also said console development takes too long to time a launch around rivals. CEO Hiroki Totoki said the company has not decided on timing or price, and he indicated memory prices are expected to stay very high through Sony’s 2027 fiscal year because of supply shortages.

Where PlayStation prices stand

After two rounds of increases, the PS5 costs $649.99 in the United States, the PS5 Digital Edition costs $599.99 and the PS5 Pro costs $899.99, which is $200 above its launch price.

What the estimates suggest

Hardware leaker Kepler_L2 put the PS6’s bill of materials at about $760 in March, then raised it to around $960 in late June. Those figures cover components only, not manufacturing, shipping or retail costs. Console makers have traditionally subsidized launch hardware by about $100 to $200 per unit. Newzoo’s Manu Rosier has suggested Sony could keep the base model at a three-digit price, possibly $999.

The risk of a premium price

Ampere Analysis estimated in August that if Sony and Microsoft launched incrementally improved consoles at $1,000 in 2028, combined PS6 and Xbox Project Helix sales over five years could be up to 38% lower than sales of the PS5 and Xbox Series consoles.

It also projected the games and services market could be $3.4 billion smaller by 2031 than if the consoles cost $700, and it listed extending the current generation beyond 2028 as one option. Aldora CEO Joost van Dreunen has warned the next generation may not arrive until 2028 and said a price above $1,000 is the floor.

What else may shape upgrades

On Oct. 13, Sony announced a Japan-only Midnight Black PS5 Digital Edition at 55,000 yen, launching Nov. 19 and limited to Japanese accounts. Sony also said on July 1 that it will stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games starting in January 2028, which has raised concerns among some longtime players about moving to a pricier, digital-focused generation.

data.title: What we know about the leaked Shrek 2 Remastered game
data.description:
What do we know about Shrek 2 Remastered? A listing for the game appeared early on the Xbox store today, and it revealed that publisher Aspyr is bringing the 2004 action-adventure back with a visual overhaul. The page was later taken down.


What the leak revealed

The listing included screenshots, a pre-order trailer and a full description, but no release date. The game is expected to be announced at the ID@Xbox Showcase on Tuesday, Oct. 20, at 10 a.m. PT. News of the remaster first surfaced in September, when a batch of Steam achievements leaked.


The 5 new features

The remaster promises the following upgrades.

  1. Improved graphics, with rebuilt textures, an enhanced interface, 4K resolution and cutscenes.
  2. A new Photo Mode for capturing snapshots.
  3. A Cheat Mode that lets players unlock cheats for a smoother playthrough.
  4. Co-op for up to four players, with couch, online or mixed play.
  5. The ability to swap heroes at any time to fight enemies, beat bosses and solve puzzles with each character’s unique abilities.

About the original game

Shrek 2 first launched in 2004 and was published by Activision. It loosely follows the movie’s story, with Shrek and Fiona heading to meet the in-laws, and adds sections that go beyond the film. Players move through eleven levels as one of four characters, with goals such as guiding the three blind mice home and mini-games that include punching chickens. Reviews landed in the mid-70s, and the game shipped more than five million copies.

Will it come to Nintendo consoles?

The listing does not confirm platforms. Aspyr usually releases games on multiple platforms, so a Switch 2 and Switch version seems likely, but nothing has been announced. The remaster would also arrive ahead of Shrek 5 next year.

data.title: Capcom breach could turn into a phishing nightmare
data.description:
Capcom says no credit card data was taken. For the 11.7 million players caught in its latest breach, the bigger danger may land in their inboxes.


The Japanese video game company confirmed that hackers broke into Capcom ID, the single account system used across its online store and games, including Street Fighter 6 and the Resident Evil and Monster Hunter franchises. In total, 11,774,247 accounts worldwide were affected.


What the hackers took from Capcom ID

For nearly every affected account, the attackers accessed email addresses along with account details. Those details include the date each account was created, the time of the most recent login, how many times the user had logged in and the IP address used for that last session.

A smaller group of 43 accounts also had dates of birth, genders, countries or regions and nicknames exposed. The company said all other passwords were untouched and that no credit card information was involved. Games and online services are running normally.

Why the 196 accounts matter

The most revealing detail is the smallest number. The attackers changed the passwords on 196 accounts, apparently trying to lock their owners out. Capcom has since reset those credentials, and the affected players can log in again.

Capcom is forcing Ultimate Frame Data to take down its Street Fighter 6 section.

Capcom’s legal team says the site contains hitbox and collision data that isn’t normally accessible through regular gameplay, and that Capcom doesn’t authorize the use of modified software or analysis tools to obtain game data.

The site was asked to remove or disable access to the SF6 data by October 30. The owner, MetalMusicMan, has already taken the section offline, saying: “Not my choice, sorry everyone.”

— Pirat_Nation 🔴 (@Pirat_Nation) October 23, 2026

That shows the intruders were not just copying data. They took control of real accounts, at least briefly.

The stolen details create a second risk. An email address paired with someone’s real login history is valuable for phishing. A scammer who knows when a player last signed in and how often they play can write a fake Capcom message that looks convincing.

Capcom is warning users to be cautious of unexpected emails and messages that ask for personal information or include links and attachments. The company plans to notify affected customers in stages and has set up regional support contacts.

A timeline Capcom moved on quickly

The company detected suspicious activity and confirmed unauthorized access on Monday, Oct. 19. By the next day, it was clear that customer data had been compromised. A day after that, the company reported the incident to police and to Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission.

The company says it has identified how the attackers got in and added safeguards to stop a repeat. It has not said when the intrusion began or who was behind it, and no group has claimed responsibility, according to sources.

Capcom has been here before</st

Okay, hear me out…🚀

Either Capcom or Bloober Team should buy Dead Space IP, and make more remakes and new games.

They are the perfect candidates, since EA’s mediocre a** doesn’t wanna make games like these and focus on their god-awful shooters and sports games.

What do you think?😎

— Rino🚀 (@RinoTheBouncer) October 23, 2026

rong>

This is not the company’s first major attack. In November 2020, the ransomware group Ragnar Locker claimed to have stolen 1 terabyte of Capcom data in an incident that may have affected up to 390,000 people. Capcom later disclosed that the attackers had entered through an outdated VPN device.

The timing of the new breach is awkward. It comes as the new Street Fighter movie plays in theaters worldwide, putting one of Capcom’s oldest franchises in the spotlight. For most players, the fallout will come later, in messages that look like Capcom but are not.

data.title: Confusing Google Play update date puzzles Android users
data.description:
Why are so many Android phones suddenly claiming to run a Google Play System update from January 1, 2027, and should owners be worried? The short answer is no. The odd date appears to be a labeling mistake rather than a sign of anything wrong with the phones themselves.


The glitch has been spotted on the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Google Pixel 8 Pro and Vivo X300 Ultra, along with other Android devices. Reports on Reddit indicate it is also affecting phones running Android 12, including older models. Samsung users with the stable One UI 9.0 software reportedly received a roughly 100 MB update before noticing the date.


What is behind the strange date

Google Play System updates let Google refresh certain Android components, such as services, security elements and compatibility features, without a full operating system upgrade. The date appearing now is not a sign that Google has released a future version of Android. According to reports, it is most likely a metadata or labeling error inside the update itself. Google has not published a detailed changelog and has not explained the cause.

Does it affect performance or security

So far, there is no evidence that the incorrect date changes how phones run, how apps work or how well devices perform. It also does not mean a phone has received security patches from January 2027. The Google Play System update date is separate from both the Android version and the security patch level, so owners who want to confirm their phone is up to date should check each of those details on its own.

The real downside is confusion. With the wrong date showing, it becomes harder to tell which Google Play System update is actually installed.

How to check your update

Open Settings, then go to Security and Privacy or About Phone, depending on the device. Tap Google Play System update, review the date shown and install any update that is offered. On Samsung phones, the option is usually found under Settings, Security and privacy, Updates, then Google Play system update, though the menu path can differ by software version.

Should you reset your phone

No. Reports suggest that changing the date and time settings or resetting the phone does not correct the displayed timestamp, so a factory reset is unnecessary. Google has not said when a fix will arrive, so users can leave their phones as they are and watch for a correction in a future update.

data.title: Switch 2 cracked open: Is Mario Kart World now moddable?
data.description:
Can an AI coding agent crack one of the most locked-down game consoles on the market? A security researcher says yes. Their jailbreak of the Nintendo Switch 2 is now public, and it has Nintendo fans asking how long it will last.


The researcher, a student who posts online as pepsipu, shared a video of Mario Kart World running with extra characters added, including Peter Griffin, Hatsune Miku, Cinnamoroll and an Angry Bird. The clip suggests the exploit is real. The creator also published a detailed write-up of the process, which is a bold move given Nintendo’s aggressive legal history.


How the jailbreak was built

The project took about two weeks and relied heavily on OpenAI’s Codex coding agent. The researcher first built a test setup around both a Switch 1 and a Switch 2 so the AI could work with as little human help as possible. Remote devices sent controller inputs over USB and captured video over HDMI, while a Bluetooth switch pressed the power button whenever the console crashed and needed a restart.

i jailbroke the nintendo switch 2

so i modded cinnamoroll, peter griffin, hatsune miku, and more into Mario Kart World, a switch 2 exclusive

now watch my friends and i get cooked by bots

learn more and get the exploit https://t.co/ykjgyfrFRp https://t.co/BOcFhejRz1

— pepsipu (@pepsipu) October 22, 2026

Codex first tried the console’s browser, but that route went nowhere. It then turned to SmileBASIC 4, a $25 game-building app sold in Nintendo’s eShop. There, the AI found an integer overflow, a type of software bug, that gave it a foothold in the console’s file system services. The Mario Kart World mods came together in about a day.

What the hack can and cannot do

The exploit is tethered, which means it disappears whenever the console shuts down and must be reapplied. It is also not a full kernel-level jailbreak. Even so, it should open the door to homebrew software, game modding and deeper reverse engineering. It works on firmware version 23.0.1.

Will Nintendo respond?

Probably, and quickly. Nintendo could remove SmileBASIC 4 from its store, push out a firmware update that closes the hole, or do both. The jailbreak also arrives right after a PlayStation 5 jailbreak surfaced, which can run PS2 emulators with support for original discs.

Why it matters

The bigger story may be the method. A small team, or even one person, used an AI agent to physically operate hardware, test ideas and find a flaw in a heavily protected system. Console makers now have to assume that tools like this will speed up the hunt for weaknesses.

data.title: Could this Meta Muse flaw put private information at risk?
data.description:
Meta has temporarily suspended a sharing feature in its Muse AI assistant after cybersecurity researchers identified a privacy weakness that could make users conversations and documents easier to discover than expected.


The issue involved links generated when users asked Muse to share conversations or interactive content. Researchers found that these pages could be located through publicly available internet records, potentially exposing sensitive information without requiring an account or login.


The discovery raises questions about the privacy protections surrounding Meta’s fast growing AI product, which launched in September and quickly attracted millions of downloads.

How Meta Muse became a fast growing AI assistant

Muse debuted Sept. 8 and surpassed 5 million downloads within 22 days, according to data from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower reviewed by TechCrunch. By Oct. 20, the application had exceeded 10.9 million downloads.

Its early growth outpaced the initial download milestones of several competing AI assistants, including ChatGPT, Grok and Claude.

Muse is designed to help users complete tasks such as booking appointments, filling out forms and handling customer service interactions. The assistant aims to take a more active role in completing tasks rather than simply answering questions.

Privacy was also an important part of the product’s introduction. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg described an architecture built around an isolated virtual machine, where users’ data and credentials would be stored. A separate security agent, known as Sentinel, was designed to approve activity involving external networks and determine when additional user permission was necessary.

However, researchers soon identified concerns about the system. An earlier report highlighted a vulnerability in Muse’s security, and a subsequent investigation by cybersecurity firm Claroc uncovered another potential weakness involving shared conversations.

Researchers found thousands of discoverable links

The issue stemmed from how Muse created pages for content users chose to share.

When someone asked the assistant to share a conversation or an interactive output, Muse generated a web page that could be opened by anyone who had the link. Meta’s intended sharing process relied on those links allowing recipients to access the content.

Claroc researchers found that the links could also be discovered through passive DNS records and subdomain discovery tools. These resources can reveal information about internet domains and associated hostnames, making it possible to locate pages without receiving a link directly from the person who created them.

The researchers identified approximately 6,800 hostnames associated with shared Muse content. They examined only a few hundred pages, using an incognito browser window and no account credentials.

Among the material they encountered were a home sale budget, a note concerning a potential bank-fraud alert that included a partial account number, a small business loan application, an internal revenue review intended for a company’s chief executive and confidential preparation materials for an executive recruitment call involving an advanced AI laboratory.

The researchers said the descriptive titles included in the web addresses made it easier to identify potentially sensitive pages before opening them. Because the hostnames were recorded in publicly accessible DNS history, the links were not as difficult to locate as the team had initially anticipated.

The findings highlighted a distinction between sharing a page with a specific recipient and making a page discoverable through other means. Although access depended on having the link, the researchers found that the links themselves could be located without being given to them.

Meta pauses sharing while it reviews the findings

Meta responded to the report by pausing the conversation sharing functionality while it examined the findings and considered changes to how links could be discovered.

A company spokesperson told TheStreet that Muse automatically creates pages when users share certain outputs, which Meta calls artifacts. The company maintained that these pages are accessible to people who possess the link, while acknowledging the need to review the researchers findings.

Claroc subsequently tested 40 pages it had previously accessed without signing in. According to the firm’s Oct. 20 update, none of those pages remained accessible, and the hostnames serving their content returned error messages.

The researchers welcomed the rapid response. However, they also noted that the hostnames and associated descriptive titles remained in passive DNS history, raising questions about whether historical records could continue to reveal information about previously shared material.

Disabling access to the pages therefore addressed an immediate part of the problem, but the persistence of historical records remained a consideration.

What Muse users should understand

The incident illustrates how a sharing feature can create privacy concerns even when the underlying AI system has security controls. Content intended for a particular recipient may become more discoverable if the links are recorded in publicly accessible systems.

Users should be cautious when sharing AI-generated pages containing financial details, confidential business information or other sensitive material. They should also review the sharing settings and privacy options available in any AI service before uploading or distributing personal information.

Meta’s decision to suspend the feature while investigating the report represents an immediate response to the discovery. Whether additional safeguards will fully address the link-discovery issue will depend on the changes the company implements and how effectively they prevent similar exposure in the future.

data.title: Riot says Mel was impossible to balance. Here’s the fix
data.description:
Riot Games has announced a midscope rework for League of Legends champion Mel that removes the part of her W, Rebuttal, which reflected projectiles back at opponents. The update, announced Oct. 20, 2026, is scheduled to arrive with Patch 26.22 on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Riot said the change was needed because it had become impossible to balance Mel’s existing kit.


Why Riot is changing Mel

In its developer update, Riot said other players no longer felt Mel was a challenge they could overcome at a reasonable win rate. Riot said its experiments found the reflect worked only as an ultimate, a solution it also rejected. The company said Mel’s current ultimate, Golden Eclipse, is core to her combat pattern and that reducing its power to a basic ability would be an unacceptable trade.


Riot had already made a smaller change to Mel in February 2026. Riot said that adjustment did not resolve player frustration, which led to this larger rework.

Mel Midscope coming on November 4 ‼️

Passive:
• Reduced early game damage and duration.
• Increased scaling health and armor.

Q:
• Slightly slower.
• Less damage on the initial explosion, with more damage shifted to subsequent hits.
• Refunds a flat amount of its cooldown when hitting at least one enemy champion.

W:
• NO LONGER reflect projectiles. It will now destroy them, deal some damage back, and grant a shield and movement speed to nearby allies.

E:
• Shorter root duration against nearby enemies and longer against farther ones.

R:
• Increased cooldown reduction scaling with ability level.

— League of Legends Leaks & News (@LeagueOfLeaks) October 20, 2026

What the new Rebuttal does

Mel’s W will still destroy enemy projectiles and retaliate against them, but it will no longer reflect them. Opponents can no longer send a Seraphine ultimate back to charm the enemy team, or turn Jhin’s own Fourth Shot against him. Instead, the ability destroys projectiles and shields and speeds up nearby allies. Riot described the new W as similar to Samira’s W or Yasuo’s Wind Wall in blocking projectiles.

Changes to the rest of the kit

Riot is changing every other ability to offset the W change. The passive will lose some early-game damage and duration in exchange for more scaling health and armor. The Q, Radiant Volley, will be slightly slower and will move more of its damage from the initial explosion into later hits. The E, Solar Snare, will root shorter against nearby enemies and longer against distant ones, which Riot says should make Mel more vulnerable in some matchups while rewarding long-range skill shots.

The combo at the center of the rework

The biggest change focuses on Mel’s passive, Searing Brilliance, and her ultimate, Golden Eclipse. Riot will refund a flat amount of the Q’s cooldown when it hits at least one champion, which helps Mel build passive stacks faster. The ultimate will also gain more cooldown reduction that scales with ability level, paying off the stacks Mel gathers.

What comes next

Mel’s rework is set to land on Nov. 4, and the changes could shift her role in competitive play. Players will need to see how the new kit performs on the Public Beta Environment before judging whether Riot has solved the problem.
